# Anonymise dataset

To allow research on an anonymised dataset we need to anonymise our data. We will use the [SAFEHR policy](https://www.safehr-data.org/anonymisation-policy) in line with our local DAPR approval

## Step 1 - Read in data

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(here)

source(here("scripts/settings.R"))

df <- readRDS(file=here("data/id_dataset.rds"))
opioid_sensititvity_df <- readRDS( file=here("data/id_opioid_sensititvity_df.rds"))
readmit_sensititvity_df <- readRDS(file=here("data/id_readmit_sensititvity_df.rds"))

```

## Step 2 - Anonymise main dataset

Prior to anonymisation the dataset is de-identified with the following columns:

```{r}

column_info <- df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ class(.x)[1])) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
               names_to = "column_name", 
               values_to = "data_type")

tibble(column_info)

```

All of the columns up to `hx_sleep_apnoea` are derived from the source dataset (by joining dataframe), the following columns are derived metrics. 


## Step 2A - Removal of Identifiers

Drop identifying columns that are not needed for the subsequent analysis.

`patient_id` was the `mrn` replaced with an integer in the prior data processing step so is kept. 

```{r}

cols_to_drop <- c(
   "INDEX.x", "BirthDate", 
  "DeathDate", "Ethnicity", "PreferredLanguage", "INDEX.y", "SurgicalCaseKey", 
  "OperationInstant", "SurgicalPrioritisationCode", "PrimaryAnesthesiaTypeCode", 
  "PrimaryAnesthesiaType", "IsElectiveSurgery", "PatientDurableKey", 
  "PrimaryProcedureKey", "PrimaryProcedureCodeKey", "PrimaryService", 
  "SurgeryEncounterKey", "ProcedureName", "IsElectiveSurgery", "PrimarySurgeonDurableKey", "specialty", "primary_surgeon_grade", 
  "coded_procedures_df", "first_anaesthesia_grade", "responsible_anaesthesia_grade", "INDEX", "index_surgery_per_encounter", "number_of_operations", "PostOperativeDestination"
  
)

anon_df <- df %>% select(-all_of(cols_to_drop))

```

## Step 2B - Masking of Identifiers with random ID's

The `Anesthatist_ID` columns have been masked prior to this step by using the `DurableKey` of the staff member and renaming with an integer list. 

We require `EncounterKey` as we use it for subsetting and joins in the analysis script. We will replace with a randomised Integer. 

We will re-assign the patient_id column with a new interger that is now sampled randomly (as opposed to the sample in order of the database order.

```{r}

#Sample the unique encounterkeys, randomise the order then add an index. 
mapping_table_encounter <- data.frame(EncounterKey = unique(anon_df$EncounterKey)) %>%
  slice(sample(1:n())) %>%
  mutate(masked_id = row_number())

# 2. Join, drop original, and rename
anon_df <- anon_df %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_encounter, by = "EncounterKey") %>%
  select(-EncounterKey) %>%
  rename(EncounterKey = masked_id)

# repeat for Patient ID

mapping_table_patient_id <- data.frame(patient_id = unique(anon_df$patient_id)) %>%
  slice(sample(1:n())) %>%
  mutate(masked_id = row_number())

anon_df <- anon_df %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_patient_id, by = "patient_id") %>%
  select(-patient_id) %>%
  rename(patient_id = masked_id)


# Repeat for providers

mapping_table_provider <- data.frame(provider_id = unique(c(anon_df$FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey, anon_df$ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey ))) %>%
  slice(sample(1:n())) %>%
  mutate(masked_id = row_number())

anon_df <- anon_df %>%
  mutate(FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey = as.integer(as.character(FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey))) %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_provider, by = join_by(FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey == provider_id)) %>%
  select(-FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey) %>%
  rename(FirstAnesthesiaProviderDurableKey = masked_id) %>%
  mutate(ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey = as.integer(as.character(ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey))) %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_provider, by = join_by(ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey == provider_id)) %>%
  select(-ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey) %>%
  rename(ResponsibleAnesthesiologistDurableKey = masked_id)







```

All other ID numbers including the patient ID have been dropped. 

## Step 2C Shifting of dates

We use the various date columns to derive important time durations (Length of surgery, length of admission). We will shift dates by a random duration sampled from a uniform distribution. We will then apply the same duration to each date column in that row using `rowwise()` to ensure that the time intervals are kept consistant. We will use +/- 5 weeks as the duration to sample from.  

We use this approach to preserve the time based features (eg rate of cobaliton by year) as opposed to anchoring to dates. 

```{r}

gen_interval <- function(weeks){
  # Sample the scalar value
  sampled_value <- runif(1, min = -weeks, max = weeks)
  # Return as a lubridate duration (defaults to seconds)
  return(dweeks(sampled_value))
}


# Generate a random interval for each row

date_cols <- c("TouchTimeStartInstant", "TouchTimeEndInstant",
              "InRecoveryInstantTracking","InRecoveryInstantTracking",
              "RecoveryCareCompleteInstantTracking","OutofRecoveryInstantTracking"  )

anon_df <- anon_df %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    diff_time = gen_interval(5), 
    across(all_of(date_cols), ~ .x + diff_time)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-diff_time)

```


## Step 2D - Jittering of numerics

We do not require to jitter the demographics listed in the SAFEHR website (Weight, BMI, etc).

The remaining numerics are as follows:

- `Length of admission`

- `Procedure length`

We have not jittered them as we determine they are not identifiable.

## Step 2E - High risk item checklist

A check of the high risk item check-list as per the (SAFEHR slab)[https://uclh.slab.com/posts/high-risk-items-3pezmyef].

- Mental health diagnosis -> Clear

- Sexual health diagnosis/tests/referals -> Clear

- Safeguarding referrals-> Clear

- DALT referrals -> clear

The high risk data items included are:

- *Gender identity and Sex* This may be used to detect a mismatch and assumed gender different to sex at birth. 

- *History of opioid dependance*

We will leave this in as they core to the dataset. 

Gender and Opiods seems reasonable (from Stef)

## Step 2F - Minimum group size supression

This is not applicable to this stage. This is a process completed at the review of the analysis to ensure that the demographics (and others) are not reporting values <5 that may reveal identifiable features.. 


# Step 3 - Anonymisation of sensativity datasets

As part of the primary analysis we produce two sensitivity analysis. 
First the the time from discharge to readmission, the second was the time from recovery to the first opioid dose. 

In these datasets we only record a vector of difftimes with the patient ID number (to identify repeat doses/admissions for a given patient). 

We will use the mapping tables produced earlier. 

```{r}

opioid_sensititvity_df <- opioid_sensititvity_df %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_encounter, by = "EncounterKey") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-EncounterKey) %>%
  rename(EncounterKey = masked_id)


head(opioid_sensititvity_df)

readmit_sensititvity_df <- readmit_sensititvity_df %>%
  left_join(mapping_table_patient_id, by = c("PatientDurableKey" = "patient_id")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-PatientDurableKey) %>%
  rename(PatientDurableKey = masked_id)

head(readmit_sensititvity_df)

```


# Step 4 - Write dataset

We now write the dataset, with the `anon_` prefix.

```{r write dataset}

saveRDS(anon_df, file=here("data/anon_dataset.rds"))

saveRDS(opioid_sensititvity_df, file=here("data/anon_opioid_sensititvity_df.rds"))

saveRDS(readmit_sensititvity_df, file=here("data/anon_readmit_sensititvity_df.rds"))

```
